Choose one or more rooms to follow. The clock shows music playing in each selected room’s group; rooms in the same group appear once.

While music plays, tap once to switch between the complete clock and song information. Double-tap at any time to exit to the Home screen.
Song recognition test
Play a record or CD at your usual listening volume, then listen for a song.

This test uses the tablet microphone for %1$d seconds and sends that sample to your selected recognition service to identify the music. The app keeps no recording. Listening stops if you leave this screen. Account and trial limits apply.

Line-In song recognition
Identify Line-In music

While the clock is visible, identify Line-In music playing in followed Living Room or Kitchen. About once a minute, the microphone samples 10 seconds for AudD or 15 seconds for AudioTag and sends the sample to that service. The app keeps no recording.
Allow microphone access to identify Line-In music. If access was previously denied, enable it in Android app permissions.

YouTube Music recognition test
Test YouTube Music
Identify one song now without changing automatic recognition.
Play music near the tablet, enable the YouTube Music bridge, then run the test. The clock stays visible while YouTube Music identifies one song.

The bridge reads only YouTube Music’s window, using screen text or on-device OCR. It keeps just the identified song and artist. YouTube Music handles listening; Farragut Clock records no audio and saves no screenshots.
This test needs Android 14 or newer to read the YouTube Music window.
Install and enable YouTube Music on this tablet before running the test.
